description: Rep Scott Peters (CA-50) seeks a Field Representative/Caseworker for the district office. description: The Committee on Ethics seeks an experienced investigative professional for a Senior Investigator position. The Committee's senior investigator will be responsible for assisting the Committee in all aspects of its investigative work, including public source research, legal research, forensic accounting, document review, data collection and analysis, witness interviews, and investigative reports. This is a nonpartisan position which requires the ability to assist with impartial investigations and refrain from political or partisan activity. Candidates must possess outstanding organizational, research, and analytical skills, as well as the sound judgment necessary to evaluate the sensitive matters that arise before the Committee. Experience in one or more of the following areas is desirable: auditing, financial accounting, fraud examination, law enforcement, government ethics, campaign finance, background investigations, victim outreach, and legal services. The salary range for this position is $125,845 to $138,024. Please email resume, cover letter, and a short writing sample to ethicsjobs@mail.house.gov. Please include the phrase "Senior Investigator" in the subject line.

description: Congresswoman Maxine Dexter is a physician, a founding member of the Democratic Doctors Caucus, and one of Congress's most committed voices on healthcare, climate, immigrant rights, and working families. Her office is seeking an experienced, creative, and strategic Communications Director in her Washington, D.C. office. This is a senior role with real creative authority. You will set the communications agenda, shape the Congresswoman's public voice, manage a small and talented team, and be a key thought partner to the Chief of Staff, Legislative Director, and District Director. The ability to maintain a flexible schedule, including evenings and weekends as necessary—with the ability to flex time during slower periods—is essential. Dexter's Portland-based district is highly engaged, and her communications operation needs to match that energy. This is a fun office that moves fast, takes the work seriously, and believes that good communication is itself a form of advocacy. This is not an entry-level position. Salary starts at $95,000 and is commensurate with experience and qualifications. The office also offers a competitive package of benefits (health insurance, student loan repayment, and more).

Manage the Congresswoman's franked communications program, including direct mail, digital advertising, mass texts, and monthly telephone town halls, ensuring full compliance with franking regulations.

Collaborate with legislative staff to translate bill introductions, legislative victories, and Floor activity into compelling public narratives.
Proactively work with the District Office to publicize Oregon-based events including town halls and community conversations.
Supervise and mentor a Digital Manager (D.C.) and part-time Press Assistant (Portland).
Respond rapidly to breaking news at the national and district level.

Monitor and engage emerging and new media platforms — including YouTube, Substack, and podcasts — identifying opportunities to expand the Congresswoman's reach and connect with audiences beyond traditional press.
Support video production, graphic design, and photography — our Digital Manager leads on most content creation, but a CD who can backstop in a pinch is essential.

Strong writing skills with the ability to draft floor speeches, press statements, op-eds, talking points, and social content on deadline.
Experience managing and mentoring staff.
Ability to maintain a flexible schedule including evenings and weekends.
Familiarity with franking regulations and compliance.
Experience with video production, graphic design, and photography is a plus.

description: Congressman Ro Khanna's district office in Santa Clara has an immediate opening for a Caseworker/Field Representative, which involves both casework and community outreach. This is a non-supervisory position. The starting salary is $71,000 per year. The application process may include several interviews and a practical test of relevant skills. This position ends on November 6, 2026 with the option to extend depending on office needs and available budget. The Caseworker/Field Representative is a represented position, part of the Congressional Workers Union, and reports to the District Director and Director of Constituent Services, or their designees. Work is mainly performed in an office environment. The district office functions on a hybrid basis, with each staff member expected to be based in the physical office three days a week and allowed to work from home two days a week. The office is open 9:00am-5:00pm Monday-Friday, with a full lunch hour. Staff can expect to work 2-3 times per week after hours on community events. Commensurate flex time will be granted upon request. Benefits include 15 days annual leave per year, 15 annual Sick/Mental Health Days, flex time, group health insurance, retirement savings, and a potential annual bonus.

description: The House Office of the Legislative Counsel (HOLC) is looking to hire up to two full-time Attorneys. Appointments to all positions in HOLC are made without regard to personal political affiliation and solely on the basis of fitness to perform the work. Attorneys at HOLC assist the United States House of Representatives, and its Committees and Members, in drafting legislation and performing related legal functions on a nonpartisan basis. The legal issues encountered in furnishing this assistance involve constitutional, statutory, and administrative law questions, as well as questions in other fields of Federal law.
responsibilities: Drafts legislation and prepares bills according to statutory style and format standards.
Drafts bills and amendments at each stage of the legislative process, from introduction through conference.
Analyzes policy proposals, engages with clients, applies relevant legal principles and court decisions, and conducts research as necessary to prepare effective statutory language.
Advises clients regarding the legal effect and constitutionality of proposed legislative measures in the context of existing laws and legislative procedure.

Attends sessions of a subcommittee and full committee of the House and of a conference committee between the House and the Senate; may respond as requested to questions from legislators and legislative staff; may assist members by being present to provide drafting assistance to members on the House Floor.
May communicate with various stakeholders, at the request of the Member or Committee, as necessary to draft legislation.
After gaining necessary experience, trains newly hired attorneys, provides mentorship to team members, and may assume a leadership role on teams.
On a volunteer basis, may assist with office management initiatives to promote the effective operation of the office.
Performs related duties as assigned.
qualifications: United States citizenship.
Graduation from a law school accredited by the American Bar Association prior to the commencement of employment.
Some experience performing legal work, which may be satisfied by employment during law school.
Active membership in the bar of a State, the District of Columbia, or a territory of the United States within one year of employment as a full-time attorney.
Strong written and oral communication skills.
Ability to remain impartial at all times with respect to the policies to be incorporated into a legislative proposal.
Ability to analyze complex problems and handle difficult situations with judgment, tact, and discretion.
Excellent problem-solving skills.
Strong interest in learning within a high-performing environment.
Demonstrated commitment to nonpartisan public service and a strong academic background.
how_to_apply: Interested and qualified candidates apply here by Friday, June 5th, for consideration. Submit your résumé, cover letter, a legal writing sample of no more than 10 pages, a copy of your law school transcript, and the names, telephone numbers, and email addresses of at least three references. Either your cover letter or résumé should indicate your citizenship. Within the cover letter, directly answer: (1) What specifically interests you about this position and why would you like to work with HOLC? (2) Have you held an internship, fellowship, or similar position (paid or unpaid) in a partisan office? If so, did you seek out the placement, or were you placed there by your school or sponsoring organization? Provide relevant details and responsibilities. Your résumé should reflect years and months of employment and/or relevant legal experience.
